newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen losing steam as summer sets in.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen losing steam as summer sets in.

text.p: The Polish bourse is seen flat or down next week in continued low summer turnovers and added uncertainty due to September's parliamentary elections and a mixed macroeconomic environment, analysts said.

They said the market had been cheered by the main WIG index's 3.4 percent late-week jump, pushing the WIG up 2.8 percent on the week to 15,572.8, but low turnovers and mixed trade after Friday's fixing augured a flatter market next week.

"It seems current gains represent a speculative rebound -- the market was so oversold...and the turnovers don't suggest the gains happened along with significant money," said Grzegorz Cimochowski, an analyst at ING Baring Securities in Warsaw.
The market had fallen to nearly 15,000 points earlier this week from about 16,500 points in mid-June.

Analysts said foreign investors were likely staying away in the run-up to the September 21 elections in which the right- wing opposition Solidarity Election Action (AWS) are seen vying for victory with the main party in the governing coalition, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD).

They said political uncertainty had been compounded by economic uncertainty reflected in the increased likelihood of a rate rise voiced this week by the central bank to counter monetary growth from 1998's planned 1.9 percent budget gap.
Analysts also said the recent slip by the zloty relative to foreign currencies was helping dampen foreign buying.

"The 5.5-percent GDP assumption in 1998's budget suggests Poland should be looked on favourably from abroad, but it seems the currency risk effectively limits the flow of foreign currency to Poland," said Pawel Demczuk of Wood & Company.
Analysts said a good sign was that the market had put behind it its largest public offerings ever, those of Bank Handlowy SA BAHAs.WA and copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA.

This weekend shares in KGHM's domestic large-investor non-preferred tranche and domestic large-investor preferred tranche will be allotted at special bourse sessions from a minimum price of 19.5 zlotys.

Analysts said Handlowy, which rose nine percent this week to 41.3 zlotys after starting trade on Monday 8.3 percent above issue, still had room to rise on Monday, although upside was limited with the GDR price now around $12.8.
